result.summary: Adds `#include <util/check.h>` and removes `<cassert>` across unit, Qt, IPC, and wallet test files using a scripted diff. A second scripted commit sorts modified include blocks using clang-format. The changes ensure test code explicitly pulls in Bitcoin Core assertion definitions.
result.problem: Tests frequently invoke assertions without directly including `util/check.h`, creating confusion over whether standard `cassert` macros subject to `NDEBUG` are active and causing issues for Include-What-You-Use (IWYU) tooling.
evidence: Commit fab3f83f9a notes: 'The project has a compile error when compiled without assertions in util/check.h. Thus, util/check.h should be included for all assertions.'

PR description notes: 'sometimes confusion arises, when it is unclear whether NDEBUG can disable the assertions, or whether to use assert or Assert. Avoid that confusion in test code with a scripted replacement to add the util/check.h include. The changes here will also make it easier to run IWYU.'
result.scope_notes: The entire PR is mechanical, consisting of two scripted-diff commits modifying includes across 51 test files.
result.changed_since_previous: Diff was previously omitted (nopatch); the implementation and commit structure remain unchanged.
result.card: Adds `#include <util/check.h>` and strips `<cassert>` across 51 unit, Qt, IPC, and wallet test files via a scripted diff, followed by an include sorting pass. This addresses ambiguity over whether assertions in tests can be disabled by NDEBUG and improves compatibility with automated Include-What-You-Use (IWYU) passes. The author notes that building without assertions in util/check.h leads to compile errors. The change is entirely mechanical and restricted to test code.

risk.why: A mistake in header includes in test files would at most cause test compilation failures.
